newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lernout & Hauspie to issue convertible pref shares.
newsitem.headline: Lernout & Hauspie to issue convertible pref shares.

text.p: Belgian, Nasdaq-listed speech technology firm Lernout & Hauspie Speech Products NV said on Wednesday it planned to issue $32 million in non-dividend bearing preferred stock which could be converted into common shares.

"The preferred stock will be convertible to common stock at a discount of three percent to the market price. On current market conditions, the number of shares issued would be approximately 1.25 million," L&H said.
The preferred stock will be issued through a private placement to which L&H Holding NV could subscribe to $8 million.
L&H said the proceeds of the placement, plus recently negotiated bank credit lines amounting to $17 million and the company's "strong cash position", would cover the cost of recent acquisitions.

The company said on Wednesday it was buying German speech translation machine maker GMS for $14.7 million in cash and new shares. In April it said it would pay $53 million in cash and new shares for speech firm Kurzweil.
A Lernout spokeswoman was not immediately available to say how many new common shares might also be issued as a result of the two acquisitions.
Lernout said, however, the GMS acquisition would not be dilutive to earnings. The Kurzweil acquisition is due to be completed by the end of June.
